stem:
Chitra writes $60 = 2\times 2\times 3\times 5$ and also $60 = 2^{2}\times 3\times 5$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer order of factors, without deciding whether the two prime factorisations are the same.
Say that having the same product $60$ is what creates the matching primes with the same repetitions.
$2\times 2\times 3\times 5$ and $2^{2}\times 3\times 5$ are the same prime factorisation; order and grouping do not change it.
Decide they differ only because one printed form uses an exponent and the other writes two $2$s.

teacher.key_rationale: A number has one prime factorisation up to order: both displays are $2^{2}\times 3\times 5$. Naming order alone, reversing product and matching primes, or judging from the exponent print form miss uniqueness.
